note_sections.t: A PSA elevation to 6.4 ng/mL alongside a previously positive biopsy bucket prompts this clinical evaluation.

A 63-year-old retired mechanical engineer entered clinical evaluation after an incidental PSA elevation surfaced during a routine wellness screening. He shares a home with his spouse and maintains a strictly alcohol-free lifestyle, abstaining from tobacco as well. A daily twenty-minute walking regimen supports his general fitness. Lower urinary tract symptoms remain mild, quantified by an IPSS score of 8, with occasional nocturia but no significant daytime urgency. Public transit limitations dictate his preference for morning consultations. His medical background is otherwise clear, aside from a laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed in 2015, and he currently uses no regular prescriptions. He reports no bone pain, unexplained weight loss, or alterations in bowel habits, maintaining a stable baseline of general well-being.

DRE: Normal. The prostate exhibits symmetrical enlargement with a smooth, rubbery consistency, lacking palpable nodules or asymmetry. General examination remains unremarkable, with stable vital signs and normal cardiovascular and pulmonary assessments. Abdominal palpation reveals a soft, non-tender abdomen devoid of masses or organomegaly.
